cards.title: Stable Angina
cards.front: What are the immediate high-yield clues for stable angina?
cards.primary_answer: Exertional chest pain relieved by rest or nitroglycerin
cards.key_finding: ST depression ± T-wave inversion during attack; ECG at rest usually normal
consequences: Troponin normal → no myocardial necrosis
Acute relief: sublingual nitroglycerin
Prevention: beta-blocker + aspirin + statin

cards.title: Unstable Angina
cards.front: New/worsening or rest chest pain + ST depression + normal troponin → ?
cards.key_finding: ST depression ± T-wave inversion with no persistent ST elevation
consequences: Pattern: new-onset, worsening, or rest angina
Troponin remains normal → distinguishes it from NSTEMI
Initial treatment: aspirin + P2Y12 inhibitor + anticoagulation ± beta-blocker

cards.title: NSTEMI
cards.key_finding: ST depression ± T-wave inversion + elevated troponin
cards.etiology: Subendocardial infarction; subendocardium is farthest from coronary supply and exposed to high wall stress
consequences: Myocardial necrosis without ST elevation
Treatment backbone: aspirin + P2Y12 inhibitor + anticoagulation ± beta-blocker
Revascularization: early invasive strategy based on risk

cards.title: STEMI
cards.key_finding: Hyperacute T waves earliest → ST elevation classic → pathological Q waves later
cards.etiology: Acute coronary occlusion causing transmural ischemia/infarction
consequences: Troponin rises ~3–4 h, peaks ~24 h, remains elevated ~7–10 days
CK-MB useful for detecting reinfarction
Preferred reperfusion: primary PCI
Fibrinolysis if timely PCI unavailable and no contraindications
V1–V4 anterior wall → LAD; II, III, aVF inferior wall → usually RCA

cards.title: MI Mechanical Complications
cards.front: What are the classic post-MI mechanical complication patterns?
cards.primary_answer: Papillary muscle rupture, ventricular septal rupture, free-wall rupture, ventricular aneurysm
cards.key_finding: Major mechanical complications classically occur about 3–7 days after MI
cards.etiology: Necrotic myocardium weakens and fails structurally
consequences: Sudden pulmonary edema + new apical holosystolic murmur → papillary muscle rupture → acute MR
New holosystolic murmur at left sternal border + O2 step-up → ventricular septal rupture
Hypotension + JVD + PEA → free-wall rupture → tamponade
Persistent ST elevation weeks later → ventricular aneurysm

cards.title: Aortic Stenosis
cards.front: What is the characteristic murmur of aortic stenosis?
cards.key_finding: Best heard at right 2nd intercostal space / RUSB and radiates to carotids
cards.etiology: Degenerative calcification in older adults; bicuspid valve in younger patients
consequences: Classic triad: angina, syncope, dyspnea
Severe AS: pulsus parvus et tardus
Chronic AS → left ventricular hypertrophy

cards.title: Mitral Regurgitation
cards.front: What is the characteristic murmur of mitral regurgitation?
cards.primary_answer: Holosystolic murmur radiating to the axilla
cards.key_finding: Best heard at the cardiac apex; radiates to axilla
cards.etiology: Mitral valve prolapse, rheumatic disease, papillary muscle dysfunction/rupture, infective endocarditis
consequences: Post-MI acute MR → papillary muscle rupture
Chronic MR → left atrial enlargement
Left atrial enlargement → atrial fibrillation
Can progress to pulmonary venous congestion, pulmonary hypertension, and late RV failure

cards.title: Mitral Stenosis
cards.front: What is the characteristic murmur of mitral stenosis?
cards.key_finding: Shorter S2–opening snap interval means more severe mitral stenosis
consequences: Left atrial enlargement
Atrial fibrillation
Left atrial thrombus
Systemic embolization → increased stroke risk
Pulmonary hypertension
Hemoptysis may reflect pulmonary venous hypertension

cards.title: IE — Organisms & Valve Associations
cards.front: What are the immediate organism clues for infective endocarditis?
cards.primary_answer: Match the exposure to the organism
cards.key_finding: Risk factor is the fastest way to identify the likely organism
cards.etiology: Bacterial colonization of damaged valve endothelium
consequences: IV drug use + fever + new murmur → Staphylococcus aureus
IV drug use most commonly involves tricuspid valve
Dental procedure + subacute endocarditis → viridans streptococci
GI/GU procedure → Enterococcus
Prosthetic valve → Staphylococcus epidermidis
Culture-negative endocarditis: remember HACEK organisms

cards.title: IE — Peripheral Findings
cards.front: What are the classic peripheral findings of infective endocarditis?
cards.primary_answer: Osler nodes, Janeway lesions, Roth spots, splinter hemorrhages
cards.etiology: Immune complex deposition and septic microemboli
consequences: Painful nodules on fingers → Osler nodes
Painless lesions on palms/soles → Janeway lesions
Retinal hemorrhages with pale centers → Roth spots
Linear hemorrhages under nails → splinter hemorrhages
New murmur often means new valvular regurgitation from valve destruction

cards.title: ACS Rapid Recognition
cards.front: How do you immediately distinguish the major ACS patterns?
cards.key_finding: ST direction and troponin status separate the ACS entities quickly
consequences: Exertional chest pain + normal troponin → stable angina
Rest/worsening chest pain + ST depression + normal troponin → unstable angina
ST depression + elevated troponin → NSTEMI
ST elevation + elevated troponin → STEMI
STEMI requires immediate reperfusion; primary PCI preferred

cards.title: Valve Murmur Rapid Recognition
cards.front: How do you immediately recognize the classic valve murmurs?
cards.key_finding: Three anchor patterns cover the classic IFOM valve questions
consequences: RUSB → carotids → crescendo-decrescendo systolic → aortic stenosis
Apex → axilla → holosystolic → mitral regurgitation
Opening snap → diastolic rumble → mitral stenosis

cards.title: Post-MI Rapid Recognition
cards.front: What are the immediate post-MI complication clues?
cards.primary_answer: Use timing + new murmur + hemodynamic collapse
cards.key_finding: Mechanical complications usually cluster 3–7 days after MI
consequences: Pulmonary edema + new apical holosystolic murmur → papillary muscle rupture → acute MR
LSB holosystolic murmur + O2 step-up → ventricular septal rupture
Hypotension + JVD + PEA → free-wall rupture → tamponade
Persistent ST elevation weeks later → ventricular aneurysm

cards.title: Endocarditis Rapid Recognition
cards.front: What are the immediate infective endocarditis associations?
cards.key_finding: This is a pure association card for fast review
consequences: IV drug use → S. aureus
Dental procedure → viridans streptococci
GI/GU procedure → Enterococcus
Prosthetic valve → S. epidermidis
Osler painful; Janeway painless
